# amq-protocol-uri 10.6.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/amq-protocol-uri/latest

**AMQP 0-9-1 protocol codec and TCP/TLS connection layer for Rust.**

This workspace provides the low-level AMQP 0-9-1 building blocks used by
[lapin](https://docs.rs/lapin). It is split into focused sub-crates that can
also be used independently.

## Crates in this workspace

Most users should depend on `amq-protocol` directly — it re-exports everything
and wires up the sub-crates. Depend on a sub-crate only when you need a strict
subset of the functionality.

## Feature flags

### Async runtime (pick exactly one)

| Flag | Notes |
| `tokio`*(default)* | Requires a running Tokio runtime |
| `smol` | Uses the smol executor |
| `async-global-executor` | Uses async-global-executor |

### TLS backend (pick at most one)

| Flag | Notes |
| `rustls`*(default)* | TLS via rustls |
| `native-tls` | TLS via the platform's native library |
| `openssl` | TLS via OpenSSL |

### Rustls certificate store (when `rustls` is active)

| Flag | Notes |
| `rustls-platform-verifier`*(default)* | Uses the platform trust store |
| `rustls-native-certs` | Loads native root certificates |
| `rustls-webpki-roots-certs` | Uses the webpki bundled root set |

### Rustls crypto provider (at least one required)

| Flag | Notes |
| `rustls--aws_lc_rs`*(default)* | Uses aws-lc-rs |
| `rustls--ring` | Uses ring (more portable, e.g. builds on Windows) |

### Miscellaneous

| Flag | Notes |
| `codegen` | Force protocol code regeneration at build time |
| `verbose-errors` | More detailed AMQP parser error messages |
| `hickory-dns` | Hickory DNS resolver (avoids spurious network hangs) |

# amq_protocol_types - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/amq-protocol-types/=10.6.2/

## Expand description

AMQP 0-9-1 type system for Rust.

Implements the full set of AMQP scalar types ([ AMQPValue](https://docs.rs/enum.AMQPValue.html),

[), compound types (](https://docs.rs/enum.AMQPType.html)

`AMQPType`[,](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldTable.html)

`FieldTable`[), and wire-format serialisation/deserialisation via the](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldArray.html)

`FieldArray`[and](https://docs.rs/generation/index.html)

`generation`[modules.](https://docs.rs/parsing/index.html)

`parsing`## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- Parsing utilities for the various AMQP types.

# percent_encoding - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/percent-encoding/^2.0/

## Expand description

URLs use special characters to indicate the parts of the request.
For example, a `?` question mark marks the end of a path and the start of a query string.
In order for that character to exist inside a path, it needs to be encoded differently.

Percent encoding replaces reserved characters with the `%` escape character
followed by a byte value as two hexadecimal digits.
For example, an ASCII space is replaced with `%20`.

When encoding, the set of characters that can (and should, for readability) be left alone
depends on the context.
The `?` question mark mentioned above is not a separator when used literally
inside of a query string, and therefore does not need to be encoded.
The [ AsciiSet](https://docs.rs/struct.AsciiSet.html) parameter of

[and](https://docs.rs/fn.percent_encode.html)

`percent_encode`[lets callers configure this.](https://docs.rs/fn.utf8_percent_encode.html)

`utf8_percent_encode`This crate deliberately does not provide many different sets.
Users should consider in what context the encoded string will be used,
read relevant specifications, and define their own set.
This is done by using the `add` method of an existing set.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use percent_encoding::{utf8_percent_encode, AsciiSet, CONTROLS};
/// https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#fragment-percent-encode-set
const FRAGMENT: &AsciiSet = &CONTROLS.add(b' ').add(b'"').add(b'<').add(b'>').add(b'`');
assert_eq!(utf8_percent_encode("foo <bar>", FRAGMENT).to_string(), "foo%20%3Cbar%3E");
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Ascii](https://docs.rs/struct.AsciiSet.html)- Set
- Represents a set of characters or bytes in the ASCII range.
- [Percent](https://docs.rs/struct.PercentDecode.html)- Decode
- The return type of `percent_decode`
- [Percent](https://docs.rs/struct.PercentEncode.html)- Encode
- The return type of `percent_encode``utf8_percent_encode`

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [CONTROLS](https://docs.rs/constant.CONTROLS.html)
- The set of 0x00 to 0x1F (C0 controls), and 0x7F (DEL).
- [NON_](https://docs.rs/constant.NON_ALPHANUMERIC.html)- ALPHANUMERIC
- Everything that is not an ASCII letter or digit.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [percent_](https://docs.rs/fn.percent_decode.html)- decode
- Percent-decode the given bytes.
- [percent_](https://docs.rs/fn.percent_decode_str.html)- decode_ - str
- Percent-decode the given string.
- [percent_](https://docs.rs/fn.percent_encode.html)- encode
- Percent-encode the given bytes with the given set.
- [percent_](https://docs.rs/fn.percent_encode_byte.html)- encode_ - byte
- Return the percent-encoding of the given byte.
- [utf8_](https://docs.rs/fn.utf8_percent_encode.html)- percent_ - encode
- Percent-encode the UTF-8 encoding of the given string.

# url - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/url/^2.0/

## Expand description

rust-url is an implementation of the [URL Standard](http://url.spec.whatwg.org/)
for the [Rust](http://rust-lang.org/) programming language.

[§](https://docs.rs#url-parsing-and-data-structures)URL parsing and data structures

First, URL parsing may fail for various reasons and therefore returns a `Result`.

```
use url::{Url, ParseError};
assert!(Url::parse("http://[:::1]") == Err(ParseError::InvalidIpv6Address))
```
Let’s parse a valid URL and look at its components.

```
use url::{Url, Host, Position};
let issue_list_url = Url::parse(
    "https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues?labels=E-easy&state=open"
)?;
assert!(issue_list_url.scheme() == "https");
assert!(issue_list_url.username() == "");
assert!(issue_list_url.password() == None);
assert!(issue_list_url.host_str() == Some("github.com"));
assert!(issue_list_url.host() == Some(Host::Domain("github.com")));
assert!(issue_list_url.port() == None);
assert!(issue_list_url.path() == "/rust-lang/rust/issues");
assert!(issue_list_url.path_segments().map(|c| c.collect::<Vec<_>>()) ==
        Some(vec!["rust-lang", "rust", "issues"]));
assert!(issue_list_url.query() == Some("labels=E-easy&state=open"));
assert!(&issue_list_url[Position::BeforePath..] == "/rust-lang/rust/issues?labels=E-easy&state=open");
assert!(issue_list_url.fragment() == None);
assert!(!issue_list_url.cannot_be_a_base());
```
Some URLs are said to be *cannot-be-a-base*:
they don’t have a username, password, host, or port,
and their “path” is an arbitrary string rather than slash-separated segments:

```
use url::Url;
let data_url = Url::parse("data:text/plain,Hello?World#")?;
assert!(data_url.cannot_be_a_base());
assert!(data_url.scheme() == "data");
assert!(data_url.path() == "text/plain,Hello");
assert!(data_url.path_segments().is_none());
assert!(data_url.query() == Some("World"));
assert!(data_url.fragment() == Some(""));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#default-features)Default Features

Versions `<= 2.5.2` of the crate have no default features. Versions `> 2.5.2` have the default feature ‘std’.
If you are upgrading across this boundary and you have specified `default-features = false`, then
you will need to add the ‘std’ feature or the ‘alloc’ feature to your dependency.
The ‘std’ feature has the same behavior as the previous versions. The ‘alloc’ feature
provides no_std support.

[§](https://docs.rs#serde)Serde

Enable the `serde` feature to include `Deserialize` and `Serialize` implementations for `url::Url`.

[§](https://docs.rs#base-url)Base URL

Many contexts allow URL *references* that can be relative to a *base URL*:

`<link rel="stylesheet" href="../main.css">`Since parsed URLs are absolute, giving a base is required for parsing relative URLs:

```
use url::{Url, ParseError};
assert!(Url::parse("../main.css") == Err(ParseError::RelativeUrlWithoutBase))
```
Use the `join` method on an `Url` to use it as a base URL:

```
use url::Url;
let this_document = Url::parse("http://servo.github.io/rust-url/url/index.html")?;
let css_url = this_document.join("../main.css")?;
assert_eq!(css_url.as_str(), "http://servo.github.io/rust-url/main.css");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#feature-serde)Feature: `serde`

If you enable the `serde` feature, [ Url](https://docs.rs/struct.Url.html) will implement

[and](https://docs.rs/serde/1/serde/trait.Serialize.html)

`serde::Serialize`[. See](https://docs.rs/serde/1/serde/trait.Deserialize.html)

`serde::Deserialize`[serde documentation](https://serde.rs)for more information.

`url = { version = "2", features = ["serde"] }`[§](https://docs.rs#feature-debugger_visualizer)Feature: `debugger_visualizer`

If you enable the `debugger_visualizer` feature, the `url` crate will include
a [natvis file](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/debugger/create-custom-views-of-native-objects)
for [Visual Studio](https://www.visualstudio.com/) that allows you to view
[ Url](https://docs.rs/struct.Url.html) objects in the debugger.

This feature requires Rust 1.71 or later.

`url = { version = "2", features = ["debugger_visualizer"] }`## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [form_urlencoded](https://docs.rs/form_urlencoded/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/form_urlencoded/index.html);

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Opaque](https://docs.rs/struct.OpaqueOrigin.html)- Origin
- Opaque identifier for URLs that have file or other schemes
- [Parse](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseOptions.html)- Options
- Full configuration for the URL parser.
- [Path](https://docs.rs/struct.PathSegmentsMut.html)- Segments - Mut
- Exposes methods to manipulate the path of an URL that is not cannot-be-base.
- [Url](https://docs.rs/struct.Url.html)
- A parsed URL record.
- [UrlQuery](https://docs.rs/struct.UrlQuery.html)
- Implementation detail of `Url::query_pairs_mut`. Typically not used directly.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Host](https://docs.rs/enum.Host.html)
- The host name of an URL.
- [Origin](https://docs.rs/enum.Origin.html)
- The origin of an URL
- [Parse](https://docs.rs/enum.ParseError.html)- Error
- Errors that can occur during parsing.
- [Position](https://docs.rs/enum.Position.html)
- Indicates a position within a URL based on its components.
- [Syntax](https://docs.rs/enum.SyntaxViolation.html)- Violation
- Non-fatal syntax violations that can occur during parsing.

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (c397dae80 2026-07-02)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

---

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

---

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

---

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# polkadot_node_subsystem_util - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/polkadot-node-subsystem-util/32.0.0/polkadot_node_subsystem_util/

## Expand description

Utility module for subsystems

Many subsystems have common interests such as canceling a bunch of spawned jobs, or determining what their validator ID is. These common interests are factored into this module.

This crate also reexports Prometheus metric types which are expected to be implemented by subsystems.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [availability_](https://docs.rs/availability_chunks/index.html)- chunks
- Helpers for the validator->chunk index mapping.
- [backing_](https://docs.rs/backing_implicit_view/index.html)- implicit_ - view
- A utility for managing the implicit view of the relay-chain derived from active leaves and the minimum allowed relay-parents that parachain candidates can have and be backed in those leaves’ children.
- [database](https://docs.rs/database/index.html)
- Database trait for subsystem. Database trait for polkadot db.
- [inclusion_](https://docs.rs/inclusion_emulator/index.html)- emulator
- An emulator for node-side code to predict the results of on-chain parachain inclusion and predict future constraints.

- This module reexports Prometheus types and defines the `Metrics`

- These reexports are required so that external crates can use the `delegated_subsystem`macro properly.

- Requests executor parameters from the runtime effective at given relay-parent. First obtains
session index at the relay-parent, relying on the fact that it should be cached by the runtime
API caching layer even if the block itself has already been pruned. Then requests executor
parameters by session index.
Returns an error if failed to communicate to the runtime, or the parameters are not in the
storage, which should never happen.
Returns default execution parameters if the runtime doesn’t yet support `SessionExecutorParams`API call. Otherwise, returns execution parameters returned by the runtime.

# yatrosci_bio_neuro - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/yatrosci-bio-neuro/0.1.0/yatrosci_bio_neuro/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#scirs-bio-neuro)SciRS Bio-Neuro

Computational neuroscience: Hodgkin-Huxley conductances, Leaky Integrate-and-Fire dynamics, and the underlying membrane biophysics (Nernst equilibrium, Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz, passive cable constants).

Coverage (canonical formulations):

- Membrane biophysics: Nernst equilibrium potential, thermal voltage, GHK resting potential, passive-cable time and space constants
- Hodgkin-Huxley: voltage-gated Na⁺/K⁺ α/β rates, steady-state gating and time constants
- Leaky Integrate-and-Fire single-compartment dynamics

[§](https://docs.rs#references)References

- Nernst, W. (1889). Die elektromotorische Wirksamkeit der Ionen.
*Z. Phys. Chem.*4, 129–181.
- Hodgkin, A. L., & Huxley, A. F. (1952). A quantitative description of
membrane current and its application to conduction and excitation in
nerve. *J. Physiol.*117, 500–544. DOI:[10.1113/jphysiol.1952.sp004764](https://doi.org/10.1113/jphysiol.1952.sp004764)
- Goldman, D. E. (1943). Potential, impedance, and rectification in
membranes. *J. Gen. Physiol.*27, 37–60. DOI:[10.1085/jgp.27.1.37](https://doi.org/10.1085/jgp.27.1.37)
- Gerstner, W., Kistler, W. M., Naud, R., & Paninski, L. (2014).
*Neuronal Dynamics*. Cambridge University Press. DOI:[10.1017/CBO9781107447615](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9781107447615)

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [gating](https://docs.rs/gating/index.html)
- Hodgkin-Huxley steady-state gating and time constants.
- [membrane](https://docs.rs/membrane/index.html)
- Membrane biophysics: equilibrium potentials and passive cable constants.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Neuron](https://docs.rs/struct.NeuronParams.html)- Params
- Neuron model parameters

–mode=link    CC … -o lib.la objs     -> .libs/lib.a (static) + .libs/lib.so (shared) + lib.la
–mode=link    CC … -o prog objs *.la  -> resolves .lo/.la and links the program
–mode=install / –mode=clean            -> best-effort copy / rm macro_overrides  m4 macro definitions injected AFTER aclocal.m4 (so they override the project’s third-party
definitions) and BEFORE configure.ac. autoconf-rs cannot yet correctly expand some standard
third-party macros (notably pkg.m4’s PKG_CHECK_MODULES, whose internals leak
`pkg_default`/`glib_minimum` -> shell syntax errors). We replace them with clean, self-contained
shell that does the real work: run pkg-config at configure time, set PFX_CFLAGS/PFX_LIBS, and
record `@PFX_CFLAGS@`/`@PFX_LIBS@` substitutions into conf_subst.sed (consumed when config files
are created, mirroring confdefs.h -> config.h).

---

# agy_bridge - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/agy-bridge/0.5.0/agy_bridge/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#agy-bridge)agy-bridge

Build LLM agents in Rust — with tools, hooks, streaming, and multimodal input.

Rust bridge for the
[Google Antigravity SDK](https://github.com/Google-Antigravity/antigravity-sdk-python)
via [PyO3](https://pyo3.rs).

Rust’s compile-time checks make it a natural fit for vibe coding agents — schema mismatches, missing parameters, and typos in tool definitions (via

[) are caught at build time, not at runtime.](https://docs.rs#custom-tools)`#[llm_tool]`

[§](https://docs.rs#installation)Installation

Add `agy-bridge` to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[dependencies]
agy-bridge = "0.5"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread"] }
```
Install the Python SDK:

`pip install google-antigravity watchfiles`

`watchfiles`is only needed for file-change triggers; timer triggers work without it.

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

```
use agy_bridge::AgyBridge;
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), agy_bridge::error::Error> {
    agy_bridge::load_dotenv();
    let bridge = AgyBridge::builder().build()?;
    let agent = bridge.default_agent().await?;
    // Send a message and get the full reply text.
    let text = agent
        .chat("Reply with 'Hello!' and nothing else.")
        .await?
        .text()
        .await?;
    println!("{text}");
    agent.shutdown().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#streaming-responses)Streaming Responses

```
use agy_bridge::{AgyBridge, config::AgentConfig};
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), agy_bridge::error::Error> {
    agy_bridge::load_dotenv();
    let bridge = AgyBridge::builder().build()?;
    // bridge.agent() returns an AgentBuilder — chain .tools() / .hooks()
    // before .await, or .await directly for a bare agent.
    let agent = bridge
        .agent(
            AgentConfig::builder()
                .system_instructions("You are a poet.")
                .build(),
        )
        .await?;
    let mut response = agent.chat("Write a short poem about space.").await?;
    if let Some(mut stream) = response.take_text_stream() {
        while let Some(chunk) = stream.recv().await {
            print!("{chunk}");
        }
    }
    println!();
    agent.shutdown().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

[§](https://docs.rs#multimodal-content)Multimodal Content

Pass text, images, audio, video, and documents in a single chat turn:

```
use agy_bridge::{
    AgyBridge,
    content::{Content, ContentPrimitive, Image},
};
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), agy_bridge::error::Error> {
    agy_bridge::load_dotenv();
    let bridge = AgyBridge::builder().build()?;
    let agent = bridge.default_agent().await?;
    // Load an image from a file path (auto-detects MIME type):
    let image = Image::from_file("blank.png")?;
    let content = Content::Multi {
        parts: vec![
            ContentPrimitive::Text { text: "Describe this image.".into() },
            ContentPrimitive::Image(image),
        ],
    };
    let text = agent.chat(content).await?.text().await?;
    println!("{text}");
    agent.shutdown().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#custom-tools)Custom Tools

Define tools with the `#[llm_tool]` proc macro — doc comments become descriptions:

```
use agy_bridge::{AgyBridge, config::AgentConfig, prelude::*, tools::ToolRegistry};
/// Gets the current weather for a city.
#[llm_tool]
fn get_weather(
    /// The city to look up.
    city: &str,
) -> Result<String, String> {
    Ok(format!("It's sunny in {city}."))
}
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), agy_bridge::error::Error> {
    agy_bridge::load_dotenv();
    let bridge = AgyBridge::builder().build()?;
    let mut registry = ToolRegistry::new();
    registry.register(GetWeather);
    let agent = bridge
        .agent(AgentConfig::builder().build())
        .tools(registry)
        .await?;
    let text = agent.chat("What's the weather in Tokyo?").await?.text().await?;
    println!("{text}");
    agent.shutdown().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```
For full control, implement the `RustTool` trait directly:

```
use agy_bridge::tools::{JsonSchema, RustTool, ToolContext, ToolError, ToolOutput, ToolRegistry};
use serde::Deserialize;
#[derive(Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
struct SearchParams {
    /// The search query string.
    query: String,
}
struct SearchTool;
impl RustTool for SearchTool {
    type Params = SearchParams;
    const NAME: &'static str = "search";
    const DESCRIPTION: &'static str = "Search a knowledge base";
    async fn call(&self, params: Self::Params, _ctx: &ToolContext) -> Result<ToolOutput, ToolError> {
        Ok(format!("Results for: {}", params.query).into())
    }
}
let registry = ToolRegistry::new().with_tool(SearchTool);
assert_eq!(registry.definitions().len(), 1);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#mcp-integration)MCP Integration

Connect external [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) servers:

```
use agy_bridge::config::{AgentConfig, McpServer};
let server = McpServer::stdio("npx")
    .args([
        "-y",
        "@modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres",
        "postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres",
    ])
    .build();
let config = AgentConfig::builder().mcp_servers([server]).build();
assert_eq!(config.mcp_servers.len(), 1);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#hooks-and-policies)Hooks and Policies

Control agent behavior with hooks and a declarative policy system:

```
use agy_bridge::{
    AgyBridge,
    config::AgentConfig,
    hooks::{HookResult, Hooks},
};
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), agy_bridge::error::Error> {
    agy_bridge::load_dotenv();
    let bridge = AgyBridge::builder().build()?;
    // 1. Register lifecycle hooks
    let mut hooks = Hooks::new();
    hooks.on_pre_turn("turn_logger", |ctx| {
        println!("[turn {}] {}", ctx.turn_number, ctx.prompt);
    });
    hooks.on_pre_tool_call_decide("safety_gate", |ctx| {
        if ctx.tool_name == "dangerous_tool" {
            HookResult::deny("blocked by policy")
        } else {
            HookResult::allow()
        }
    });
    // 2. Create the agent configuration
    let config = AgentConfig::builder().build();
    // 3. Pass hooks to the agent builder
    let agent = bridge
        .agent(config)
        .hooks(hooks)
        .await?;
    let text = agent.chat("What is the capital of Japan?").await?.text().await?;
    println!("{text}");
    agent.shutdown().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```
```
use agy_bridge::policies::{PolicyRule, PolicySet};
let mut policies = PolicySet::new();
policies.push(PolicyRule::allow("view_file")).unwrap();
policies.push(PolicyRule::deny("run_command")).unwrap();
policies.push(PolicyRule::DenyAll).unwrap();
assert!(policies.evaluate("view_file").is_allowed());
assert!(policies.evaluate("run_command").is_denied());
assert!(policies.evaluate("unknown_tool").is_denied());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#triggers)Triggers

Run background tasks that react to timers or file changes:

```
use agy_bridge::{
    AgyBridge,
    config::AgentConfig,
    triggers::{TriggerConfig, TriggerEntry},
};
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), agy_bridge::error::Error> {
    agy_bridge::load_dotenv();
    let bridge = AgyBridge::builder().build()?;
    let periodic = TriggerEntry::new(
        "poll_status",
        TriggerConfig::every_secs(30),
        "Check deployment status",
    );
    let file_watch = TriggerEntry::new(
        "watch_workspace",
        TriggerConfig::on_file_change(std::env::current_dir()?),
        "Files changed: {changes}",
    );
    let config = AgentConfig::builder()
        .triggers(vec![periodic, file_watch])
        .build();
    let agent = bridge.agent(config).await?;
    // The agent will now automatically run triggers in the background.
    let text = agent.chat("Hello!").await?.text().await?;
    println!("{text}");
    agent.shutdown().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

Note:`on_file_change`triggers require the`watchfiles`Python package (`pip install watchfiles`). Timer triggers (`every`) work without extra dependencies.

[§](https://docs.rs#subagents)Subagents

Spawn child agents that share the parent’s runtime:

```
use agy_bridge::{AgyBridge, config::AgentConfig};
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), agy_bridge::error::Error> {
    agy_bridge::load_dotenv();
    let bridge = AgyBridge::builder().build()?;
    let parent = bridge.agent(
        AgentConfig::builder()
            .system_instructions("You are a coordinator.")
            .build(),
    ).await?;
    let child = parent.spawn_subagent(
        AgentConfig::builder()
            .system_instructions("You are a math specialist.")
            .model("gemini-3.5-flash")
            .build(),
        None,
    ).await?;
    let text = child.chat("What is 17 * 23?").await?.text().await?;
    println!("{text}");
    child.shutdown().await?;
    parent.shutdown().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

## Expand description

Inbound Queue

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

Receives messages emitted by the Gateway contract on Ethereum, whereupon they are verified, translated to XCM, and finally sent to their final destination parachain.

The message relayers are rewarded using native currency from the sovereign account of the destination parachain.

# sim_lib_surface_card - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-surface-card/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_surface_card/

## Expand description

Shared, plain-data surface-card spine.

This crate holds the codec-neutral pieces of a “surface card”: the
external-name policy used when projecting a kernel [ Symbol](https://docs.rs/sim-kernel/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_kernel/id/struct.Symbol.html)
onto a foreign tool surface (MCP, OpenAI, file system, human-facing text) and
a plain-data

[spine that depends only on kernel types.](https://docs.rs/struct.SurfaceDescriptor.html)

`SurfaceDescriptor`Concrete surfaces (for example `sim-lib-skill`’s OpenAI tool descriptor)
derive their external names through [ external_name](https://docs.rs/fn.external_name.html), keeping a single
source of truth for the mangling rules.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use sim_kernel::Symbol;
use sim_lib_surface_card::{ExternalNamePolicy, external_name};
let symbol = Symbol::qualified("skill", "do.thing");
assert_eq!(external_name(&symbol, ExternalNamePolicy::OpenAiTool), "skill_do_thing");
assert_eq!(external_name(&symbol, ExternalNamePolicy::HumanReadable), "skill/do.thing");
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Surface](https://docs.rs/struct.SurfaceDescriptor.html)- Descriptor
- Plain-data spine describing a surface (a callable projected onto a foreign tool surface). Depends only on kernel types; concrete codecs render it.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [External](https://docs.rs/enum.ExternalNamePolicy.html)- Name - Policy
- Policy selecting how a kernel `Symbol`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [external_](https://docs.rs/fn.external_name.html)- name
- Project `symbol`onto an external name according to`policy`.

# js2rust_bridge_macro - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/js2rust-bridge-macro/0.8.2/js2rust_bridge_macro/

## Expand description

Proc-macro for generating Rust FFI bindings from js2rust C ABI export metadata.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

The macro reads `js2rust.toml` from the crate root, transpiles JS to Zig,
writes output to `.js2zig-cache/{group}/`, and generates Rust FFI bindings.
The group name is derived from the file name (sanitized for Zig identifiers).
A minimal `build.rs` only needs `js2rust_bridge::build(false)`.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [js2rust_](https://docs.rs/macro.js2rust_bridge.html)- bridge
- Function-like proc-macro: `js2rust_bridge!()`.

## Attribute Macros[§](https://docs.rs#attributes)

- [host_fn](https://docs.rs/attr.host_fn.html)
- `#[host_fn]`attribute macro — eliminates unsafe C ABI plumbing from host functions.

---

# js2zig_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/js2zig-core/0.7.2/js2zig_core/

[Skip to main content](#main-content)# Crate js2zig_core

[Source](../src/js2zig_core/lib.rs.html#3-186) - [analyzer](analyzer/index.html)
- Dependency analyzer — scan all JS files, build import graph,
and partition files into groups (one core file + its transitive deps).

- Host function registry — allows JS code to call custom Rust functions.

# thingd - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/thingd/0.47.1/thingd/

## Expand description

Core primitives for thingd.

This crate owns the durable engine boundary: object storage, append-only
events, and queue storage. The default implementation is in-memory, with a
feature-gated `SQLite` adapter available for durable object, event, and
queue storage.

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature Flags

| Feature | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sqlite` | No | Enables with FTS5 search, WAL mode, and auto-migration`SqliteThingStore` |
| `connectors` | No | Enables CSV/JSON file connectors for data import |

[§](https://docs.rs#example-in-memory)Example (in-memory)

```
use thingd::{MemoryEngine, ObjectStore, EventLog, MemoryObject, MemoryEvent};
let mut engine = MemoryEngine::new();
let obj = MemoryObject::new("users", "alice", r#"{"name":"Alice"}"#);
engine.put_object(obj).unwrap();
let user = engine.get_object("users", "alice").unwrap();
assert_eq!(user.unwrap().body, r#"{"name":"Alice"}"#);
let event = MemoryEvent::new("audit", "user.created", r#"{"user":"alice"}"#);
engine.append_event(event).unwrap();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example-sqlite--requires-sqlite-feature)Example (`SQLite` — requires `sqlite` feature)

```
#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
{
    use thingd::{SqliteThingStore, ObjectStore, MemoryObject};
    let mut db = SqliteThingStore::open_in_memory().unwrap();
    db.put_object(MemoryObject::new("users", "alice", r#"{"name":"Alice"}"#)).unwrap();
    let user = db.get_object("users", "alice").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(user.unwrap().body, r#"{"name":"Alice"}"#);
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Link](https://docs.rs/struct.Link.html)
- A graph link connecting two references.
- [Link](https://docs.rs/struct.LinkQueryOptions.html)- Query - Options
- Options for querying graph links.
- [List](https://docs.rs/struct.ListEventsOptions.html)- Events - Options
- Options for listing events.
- [List](https://docs.rs/struct.ListObjectsOptions.html)- Objects - Options
- Options for listing objects in a collection.

- In-memory engine used to prove the storage boundary.
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryEvent.html)- Event
- An append-only event stored in a thingd stream.
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryObject.html)- Object
- An object stored in a thingd collection.
- [Object](https://docs.rs/struct.ObjectKey.html)- Key
- Stable object key inside a collection.
- [PutObject](https://docs.rs/struct.PutObjectOptions.html)- Options
- Options for putting an object.
- [Queue](https://docs.rs/struct.QueueClaimOptions.html)- Claim - Options
- Options used when claiming a queue job.
- [Queue](https://docs.rs/struct.QueueJob.html)- Job
- A queued unit of work.
- [Queue](https://docs.rs/struct.QueueNackOptions.html)- Nack - Options
- Options used when rejecting a leased queue job.
- [Search](https://docs.rs/struct.SearchHit.html)- Hit
- A single match returned by a search query.
- [Search](https://docs.rs/struct.SearchOptions.html)- Options
- Options used when performing a search.
- [SortBy](https://docs.rs/struct.SortBy.html)
- Sort specification for list queries.
- [Sqlite](https://docs.rs/struct.SqliteThingStore.html)- Thing - Store - `sqlite`
- `SQLite`-backed memory store.

# mmdb - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/mmdb/4.0.3/mmdb/

## Expand description

MMDB — the pure-Rust LSM-Tree storage engine behind
[vsdb](https://github.com/rust-util-collections/vsdb).

A high-performance LSM-Tree storage engine in pure Rust.

The public API is the set of items re-exported from this crate root; internal modules (WAL, SST, manifest, compaction, cache, …) are implementation details and deliberately private.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Bidi](https://docs.rs/struct.BidiIterator.html)- Iterator
- A bidirectional iterator over (user_key, value) pairs.
- [DB](https://docs.rs/struct.DB.html)
- The core database handle.
- [DBIterator](https://docs.rs/struct.DBIterator.html)
- A database-level iterator that presents a clean view of key-value pairs.
- [DbOptions](https://docs.rs/struct.DbOptions.html)
- Database-level options.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)
- The MMDB error type. See the [module documentation](https://docs.rs/self)for details.
- [Read](https://docs.rs/struct.ReadOptions.html)- Options
- Options for read operations.
- [Snapshot](https://docs.rs/struct.Snapshot.html)
- RAII snapshot guard. Automatically releases the snapshot when dropped.
- [Write](https://docs.rs/struct.WriteBatch.html)- Batch
- A write batch groups multiple mutations to be applied atomically.
- [Write](https://docs.rs/struct.WriteBatchWithIndex.html)- Batch - With - Index
- A WriteBatch with a secondary sorted index for efficient iteration. Allows iterating over batch contents merged with a DB snapshot.
- [Write](https://docs.rs/struct.WriteOptions.html)- Options
- Options for write operations.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Compaction](https://docs.rs/enum.CompactionFilterDecision.html)- Filter - Decision
- Decision returned by a compaction filter.
- [Compression](https://docs.rs/enum.CompressionType.html)- Type
- Compression type for a block.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.ErrorKind.html)- Kind
- Classifies an `Error`

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [MAX_](https://docs.rs/constant.MAX_USER_KEY_SIZE.html)- USER_ - KEY_ - SIZE
- Maximum allowed user key length for writes (8 MiB).
- [MAX_](https://docs.rs/constant.MAX_WRITE_ENTRY_SIZE.html)- WRITE_ - ENTRY_ - SIZE
- Maximum allowed user key + value payload for a single write entry.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Block](https://docs.rs/trait.BlockPropertyCollector.html)- Property - Collector
- Collects properties from key-value pairs during SST building. One instance per property type per SST file build.
- [Block](https://docs.rs/trait.BlockPropertyFilter.html)- Property - Filter
- Filters data blocks based on collected properties during iteration.
- [Compaction](https://docs.rs/trait.CompactionFilter.html)- Filter
- Trait for custom compaction filters.
- [Result](https://docs.rs/trait.ResultExt.html)- Ext
- Extension trait adding trace frames to `Result`values as they propagate.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Result](https://docs.rs/type.Result.html)
- Result type used throughout MMDB.
- [Sequence](https://docs.rs/type.SequenceNumber.html)- Number
- Global monotonically increasing sequence number.
- [Skip](https://docs.rs/type.SkipPointFn.html)- Point - Fn
- Callback that returns `true`for user keys that should be skipped during iteration.

# amq-protocol-uri 10.6.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/amq-protocol-uri/10.6.2

**AMQP 0-9-1 protocol codec and TCP/TLS connection layer for Rust.**

This workspace provides the low-level AMQP 0-9-1 building blocks used by
[lapin](https://docs.rs/lapin). It is split into focused sub-crates that can
also be used independently.

## Crates in this workspace

Most users should depend on `amq-protocol` directly — it re-exports everything
and wires up the sub-crates. Depend on a sub-crate only when you need a strict
subset of the functionality.

## Feature flags

### Async runtime (pick exactly one)

| Flag | Notes |
| `tokio`*(default)* | Requires a running Tokio runtime |
| `smol` | Uses the smol executor |
| `async-global-executor` | Uses async-global-executor |

### TLS backend (pick at most one)

| Flag | Notes |
| `rustls`*(default)* | TLS via rustls |
| `native-tls` | TLS via the platform's native library |
| `openssl` | TLS via OpenSSL |

### Rustls certificate store (when `rustls` is active)

| Flag | Notes |
| `rustls-platform-verifier`*(default)* | Uses the platform trust store |
| `rustls-native-certs` | Loads native root certificates |
| `rustls-webpki-roots-certs` | Uses the webpki bundled root set |

### Rustls crypto provider (at least one required)

| Flag | Notes |
| `rustls--aws_lc_rs`*(default)* | Uses aws-lc-rs |
| `rustls--ring` | Uses ring (more portable, e.g. builds on Windows) |

### Miscellaneous

| Flag | Notes |
| `codegen` | Force protocol code regeneration at build time |
| `verbose-errors` | More detailed AMQP parser error messages |
| `hickory-dns` | Hickory DNS resolver (avoids spurious network hangs) |

---

[173](#173)fn int_queryparam<T: FromStr<Err = ParseIntError>>(
[174](#174)    url: &Url,
[175](#175)    param: &str,
[176](#176)) -> Result<Option<T>, String> {
[177](#177)    url.query_pairs()
[178](#178)        .find(|(key, _)| key == param)
[179](#179)        .map_or(Ok(None), |(_, ref value)| value.parse::<T>().map(Some))
[180](#180)        .map_err(|e: ParseIntError| e.to_string())
[181](#181)}
[182](#182)
[183](#183)impl FromStr for AMQPUri {
[184](#184)    type Err = String;
[185](#185)
[186](#186)    fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
[187](#187)        let url = Url::parse(s).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
[188](#188)        if url.cannot_be_a_base() {
[189](#189)            return Err(format!("Invalid URL: '{s}'"));
[190](#190)        }
[191](#191)        let default = AMQPUri::default();
[192](#192)        let scheme = url.scheme().parse::<AMQPScheme>()?;
[193](#193)        let username = match url.username() {
[194](#194)            "" => default.authority.userinfo.username,
[195](#195)            username => percent_decode(username)?,
[196](#196)        };
[197](#197)        let password = url
[198](#198)            .password()
[199](#199)            .map_or(Ok(default.authority.userinfo.password), percent_decode)?;
[200](#200)        let host = url
[201](#201)            .domain()
[202](#202)            .map_or(Ok(default.authority.host), percent_decode)?;
[203](#203)        let port = url.port().unwrap_or_else(|| scheme.default_port());
[204](#204)        let vhost = percent_decode(url.path().get(1..).unwrap_or("/"))?;
[205](#205)        let frame_max = int_queryparam(&url, "frame_max")?;
[206](#206)        let channel_max = int_queryparam(&url, "channel_max")?;
[207](#207)        let heartbeat = int_queryparam(&url, "heartbeat")?;
[208](#208)        let connection_timeout = int_queryparam(&url, "connection_timeout")?;
[209](#209)        let auth_mechanism = url
[210](#210)            .query_pairs()
[211](#211)            .find(|(key, _)| key == "auth_mechanism")
[212](#212)            .map_or(Ok(None), |(_, ref value)| value.parse().map(Some))?;
[213](#213)
[214](#214)        Ok(AMQPUri {
[215](#215)            scheme,
[216](#216)            authority: AMQPAuthority {
[217](#217)                userinfo: AMQPUserInfo { username, password },
[218](#218)                host,
[219](#219)                port,
[220](#220)            },
[221](#221)            vhost,
[222](#222)            query: AMQPQueryString {
[223](#223)                frame_max,
[224](#224)                channel_max,
[225](#225)                heartbeat,
[226](#226)                connection_timeout,
[227](#227)                auth_mechanism,
[228](#228)            },
[229](#229)        })
[230](#230)    }
[231](#231)}
[232](#232)
[233](#233)impl fmt::Display for AMQPUri {
[234](#234)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[235](#235)        write!(
[236](#236)            f,
[237](#237)            "{}://{}:{}@{}:{}/{}",
[238](#238)            self.scheme,
[239](#239)            percent_encode(&self.authority.userinfo.username),
[240](#240)            percent_encode(&self.authority.userinfo.password),
[241](#241)            self.authority.host,
[242](#242)            self.authority.port,
[243](#243)            percent_encode(&self.vhost),
[244](#244)        )?;
[245](#245)        let mut sep = '?';
[246](#246)        if let Some(v) = self.query.frame_max {
[247](#247)            write!(f, "{sep}frame_max={v}")?;
[248](#248)            sep = '&';
[249](#249)        }
[250](#250)        if let Some(v) = self.query.channel_max {
[251](#251)            write!(f, "{sep}channel_max={v}")?;
[252](#252)            sep = '&';
[253](#253)        }
[254](#254)        if let Some(v) = self.query.heartbeat {
[255](#255)            write!(f, "{sep}heartbeat={v}")?;
[256](#256)            sep = '&';
[257](#257)        }
[258](#258)        if let Some(v) = self.query.connection_timeout {
[259](#259)            write!(f, "{sep}connection_timeout={v}")?;
[260](#260)            sep = '&';
[261](#261)        }
[262](#262)        if let Some(v) = self.query.auth_mechanism {
[263](#263)            write!(f, "{sep}auth_mechanism={v}")?;
[264](#264)        }
[265](#265)        Ok(())
[266](#266)    }
[267](#267)}

# SASLMechanism in amq_protocol_uri - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/amq-protocol-uri/10.6.2/amq_protocol_uri/enum.SASLMechanism.html

```
pub enum SASLMechanism {
    AMQPlain,
    Anonymous,
    External,
    Plain,
    RabbitCrDemo,
}
```
## Expand description

The SASL mechanisms supported by RabbitMQ

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.AMQPlain)

### AMQPlain

This is a legacy mechanism kept for backward compatibility

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Anonymous)

### Anonymous

Anonymous authentication if supported by the RabbitMQ server

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.External)

### External

Delegate all authentication to the transport instead of the RabbitMQ server

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Plain)

### Plain

Default plain login, this should be supported everywhere

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.RabbitCrDemo)

### RabbitCrDemo

A demo of RabbitMQ SecureOk mechanism, offers the same level of security as Plain

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

All the builds on docs.rs are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The limits for this crate are the following:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                    [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                    to get them increased.

# amq-protocol-types 10.6.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/amq-protocol-types/=10.6.2

**AMQP 0-9-1 protocol codec and TCP/TLS connection layer for Rust.**

This workspace provides the low-level AMQP 0-9-1 building blocks used by
[lapin](https://docs.rs/lapin). It is split into focused sub-crates that can
also be used independently.

## Crates in this workspace

Most users should depend on `amq-protocol` directly — it re-exports everything
and wires up the sub-crates. Depend on a sub-crate only when you need a strict
subset of the functionality.

## Feature flags

### Async runtime (pick exactly one)

| Flag | Notes |
| `tokio`*(default)* | Requires a running Tokio runtime |
| `smol` | Uses the smol executor |
| `async-global-executor` | Uses async-global-executor |

### TLS backend (pick at most one)

| Flag | Notes |
| `rustls`*(default)* | TLS via rustls |
| `native-tls` | TLS via the platform's native library |
| `openssl` | TLS via OpenSSL |

### Rustls certificate store (when `rustls` is active)

| Flag | Notes |
| `rustls-platform-verifier`*(default)* | Uses the platform trust store |
| `rustls-native-certs` | Loads native root certificates |
| `rustls-webpki-roots-certs` | Uses the webpki bundled root set |

### Rustls crypto provider (at least one required)

| Flag | Notes |
| `rustls--aws_lc_rs`*(default)* | Uses aws-lc-rs |
| `rustls--ring` | Uses ring (more portable, e.g. builds on Windows) |

### Miscellaneous

| Flag | Notes |
| `codegen` | Force protocol code regeneration at build time |
| `verbose-errors` | More detailed AMQP parser error messages |
| `hickory-dns` | Hickory DNS resolver (avoids spurious network hangs) |

---

# percent-encoding 2.3.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/percent-encoding/^2.0

URLs use special characters to indicate the parts of the request.
For example, a `?` question mark marks the end of a path and the start of a query string.
In order for that character to exist inside a path, it needs to be encoded differently.

Percent encoding replaces reserved characters with the `%` escape character
followed by a byte value as two hexadecimal digits.
For example, an ASCII space is replaced with `%20`.

When encoding, the set of characters that can (and should, for readability) be left alone
depends on the context.
The `?` question mark mentioned above is not a separator when used literally
inside of a query string, and therefore does not need to be encoded.
The [`AsciiSet`] parameter of [`percent_encode`] and [`utf8_percent_encode`]
lets callers configure this.

This crate deliberately does not provide many different sets.
Users should consider in what context the encoded string will be used,
read relevant specifications, and define their own set.
This is done by using the `add` method of an existing set.

# Examples

```
use ;
/// https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#fragment-percent-encode-set
const FRAGMENT: &AsciiSet = &CONTROLS.add.add.add.add.add;
assert_eq!;
```

---

# url 2.5.8 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/url/^2.0

# rust-url

URL library for Rust, based on the [URL Standard](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/).

Please see [UPGRADING.md](https://github.com/servo/rust-url/blob/main/UPGRADING.md) if you are upgrading from a previous version.

## Alternative Unicode back ends

`url` depends on the `idna` crate. By default, `idna` uses [ICU4X](https://github.com/unicode-org/icu4x/) as its Unicode back end. If you wish to opt for different tradeoffs between correctness, run-time performance, binary size, compile time, and MSRV, please see the [README of the latest version of the  idna_adapter crate](https://docs.rs/crate/idna_adapter/latest) for how to opt into a different Unicode back end.

---

# amq-protocol-uri 10.5.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/amq-protocol-uri/10.5.0

## Features

- codegen: force code generation (default to pregenerated sources)
- hickory-dns: use hickory-dns for domain name resolution to avoid spurious network hangs
- vendored-openssl: use a vendored openssl version instead of the system one (when using openssl backend)
- verbose-errors: enable more verbose errors in the AMQP parser

## Runtime

- tokio (default)
- smol
- async-global-executor

## TLS backends

- native-tls
- openssl
- rustls (default)

## Rustls certificates store

- rustls-platform-verifier (default)
- rustls-native-certs
- rustls-webpki-roots-certs

## Warning about crypto backends for rustls

A crypto implementation must be enabled in rustls using feature flags. We mimic what rustls does, providing one feature flag per implementation and enabling the same as rustls by default. Available options are:

- `rustls--aws_lc_rs`(default)
- `rustls--ring`

---

# amq_protocol - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/amq-protocol

## Expand description

AMQP 0-9-1 protocol codec for Rust.

This crate is the main entry point for the `amq-protocol` workspace. It
re-exports the [ tcp](https://docs.rs/amq-protocol-tcp/10.6.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/amq_protocol_tcp/index.html),

[, and](https://docs.rs/amq-protocol-types/10.6.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/amq_protocol_types/index.html)

`types`[sub-crates and provides the code-generated](https://docs.rs/amq-protocol-uri/10.6.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/amq_protocol_uri/index.html)

`uri`[module (produced from the RabbitMQ spec), plus](https://docs.rs/protocol/index.html)

`protocol`[helpers and](https://docs.rs/auth/index.html)

`auth`[serialisation/deserialisation utilities.](https://docs.rs/frame/index.html)

`frame`[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature flags

[§](https://docs.rs#async-runtime-pick-exactly-one)Async runtime (pick exactly one)

| Flag | Notes |
|---|---|
| `tokio`(default) | Requires a running Tokio runtime |
| `smol` | Uses the smol executor |
| `async-global-executor` | Uses async-global-executor |

[§](https://docs.rs#tls-backend-pick-at-most-one-rustls-is-the-default)TLS backend (pick at most one; `rustls` is the default)

| Flag | Notes |
|---|---|
| `rustls`(default) | TLS via rustls |
| `native-tls` | TLS via the platform’s native library |
| `openssl` | TLS via OpenSSL |

[§](https://docs.rs#rustls-certificate-store-only-when-rustls-is-active)Rustls certificate store (only when `rustls` is active)

| Flag | Notes |
|---|---|
| `rustls-platform-verifier`(default) | Uses the platform trust store |
| `rustls-native-certs` | Loads native root certificates |
| `rustls-webpki-roots-certs` | Uses the webpki bundled root set |

[§](https://docs.rs#rustls-crypto-provider-at-least-one-must-be-enabled)Rustls crypto provider (at least one must be enabled)

| Flag | Notes |
|---|---|
| `rustls--aws_lc_rs`(default) | Uses aws-lc-rs |
| `rustls--ring` | Uses ring (more portable) |

[§](https://docs.rs#miscellaneous)Miscellaneous

| Flag | Notes |
|---|---|
| `codegen` | Force protocol code regeneration at build time |
| `verbose-errors` | More detailed AMQP parser error messages |
| `hickory-dns` | Use hickory-dns for name resolution |

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [amq_protocol_tcp](https://docs.rs/amq-protocol-tcp/10.6.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/amq_protocol_tcp/index.html)as tcp;
- `pub use`- [amq_protocol_types](https://docs.rs/amq-protocol-types/10.6.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/amq_protocol_types/index.html)as types;
- `pub use`- [amq_protocol_uri](https://docs.rs/amq-protocol-uri/10.6.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/amq_protocol_uri/index.html)as uri;

---

# lapin - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lapin

## Expand description

An async AMQP 0-9-1 client library targeting RabbitMQ.

[§](https://docs.rs#core-concepts)Core concepts

`Connection`

`Channel`[. All AMQP operations (declaring queues, publishing, consuming, …) are performed through channels. Open as many as you need; they are cheap.](https://docs.rs/struct.Connection.html)

`Connection`

`Consumer``Stream` of [values obtained by calling](https://docs.rs/message/struct.Delivery.html)

`message::Delivery`[. Each delivery must be explicitly acknowledged once processed.](https://docs.rs/struct.Channel.html#method.basic_consume)

`Channel::basic_consume`

`PublisherConfirm`[that resolves to a](https://docs.rs/struct.Channel.html#method.basic_publish)

`Channel::basic_publish`[once the broker has acknowledged the message (requires](https://docs.rs/enum.Confirmation.html)

`Confirmation`[).](https://docs.rs/struct.Channel.html#method.confirm_select)

`Channel::confirm_select`[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick start

```
use async_rs::traits::Executor;
use futures_lite::stream::StreamExt;
use lapin::{
    options::*, types::FieldTable, BasicProperties, Connection,
    ConnectionProperties, Result,
};
fn main() -> Result<()> {
    let addr = std::env::var("AMQP_ADDR")
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| "amqp://127.0.0.1:5672/%2f".into());
    let runtime = lapin::runtime::default_runtime()?;
    runtime.clone().block_on(async move {
        let conn = Connection::connect(&addr, ConnectionProperties::default()).await?;
        let channel = conn.create_channel().await?;
        channel
            .queue_declare("hello".into(), QueueDeclareOptions::durable(), FieldTable::default())
            .await?;
        channel
            .basic_publish(
                "".into(),
                "hello".into(),
                BasicPublishOptions::default(),
                b"Hello, world!",
                BasicProperties::default(),
            )
            .await?
            .await?;
        let mut consumer = channel
            .basic_consume(
                "hello".into(),
                "my_consumer".into(),
                BasicConsumeOptions::default(),
                FieldTable::default(),
            )
            .await?;
        while let Some(delivery) = consumer.next().await {
            let delivery = delivery?;
            delivery.ack(BasicAckOptions::default()).await?;
        }
        Ok(())
    })
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#automatic-connection-recovery)Automatic connection recovery

Enable recovery in [ ConnectionProperties](https://docs.rs/struct.ConnectionProperties.html) to automatically reconnect and
replay topology (exchanges, queues, bindings, consumers) after a network
failure:

```
use lapin::ConnectionProperties;
let props = ConnectionProperties::default().enable_auto_recover();
// then pass `props` to Connection::connect(…)
```
After catching an error from a channel operation, call
[ Channel::wait_for_recovery](https://docs.rs/struct.Channel.html#method.wait_for_recovery) to block until the connection has been
re-established:

`channel.wait_for_recovery(error).await?;`[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature flags

[§](https://docs.rs#async-runtime-pick-exactly-one)Async runtime (pick exactly one)

| Flag | Notes |
|---|---|
| `tokio`(default) | Requires a Tokio runtime |
| `smol` | Uses the smol executor |
| `async-global-executor` | Uses async-global-executor |

[§](https://docs.rs#tls-backend-pick-at-most-one-rustls-is-the-default)TLS backend (pick at most one; `rustls` is the default)

| Flag | Notes |
|---|---|
| `rustls`(default) | TLS via rustls |
| `native-tls` | TLS via the platform’s native library |
| `openssl` | TLS via OpenSSL |

[§](https://docs.rs#rustls-certificate-store-only-when-rustls-is-active)Rustls certificate store (only when `rustls` is active)

| Flag | Notes |
|---|---|
| `rustls-platform-verifier`(default) | Uses the platform trust store |
| `rustls-native-certs` | Loads native root certificates |
| `rustls-webpki-roots-certs` | Uses the webpki bundled root set |

[§](https://docs.rs#rustls-crypto-provider-at-least-one-must-be-enabled)Rustls crypto provider (at least one must be enabled)

| Flag | Notes |
|---|---|
| `rustls--aws_lc_rs`(default) | Uses aws-lc-rs |
| `rustls--ring` | Uses ring (more portable) |

[§](https://docs.rs#miscellaneous)Miscellaneous

| Flag | Notes |
|---|---|

| `codegen` | Force code regeneration at build time |
| `verbose-errors` | More detailed AMQP parser error messages |

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [auth](https://docs.rs/auth/index.html)
- Authentication providers and helpers for connecting to RabbitMQ.
- [message](https://docs.rs/message/index.html)
- AMQP message types delivered to consumers.
- [options](https://docs.rs/options/index.html)
- Options structs for every AMQP method that accepts flag arguments.
- [protocol](https://docs.rs/protocol/index.html)
- Code-generated AMQP 0-9-1 method and property types derived from the RabbitMQ spec.
- [runtime](https://docs.rs/runtime/index.html)
- Runtime selection and helpers.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Acker](https://docs.rs/struct.Acker.html)
- Handle for acknowledging, negatively acknowledging, or rejecting a delivery.
- [Channel](https://docs.rs/struct.Channel.html)
- Main entry point for most AMQP operations.
- [Channel](https://docs.rs/struct.ChannelStatus.html)- Status
- Shared, cheaply cloneable view of a channel’s current state.
- [Configuration](https://docs.rs/struct.Configuration.html)
- The negotiated connection parameters returned by the AMQP handshake.
- [Connection](https://docs.rs/struct.Connection.html)
- A TCP connection to the AMQP server.
- [Connection](https://docs.rs/struct.ConnectionBuilder.html)- Builder
- Builder for `Connection`
- [Connection](https://docs.rs/struct.ConnectionProperties.html)- Properties
- Configuration for establishing a `Connection`
- [Connection](https://docs.rs/struct.ConnectionStatus.html)- Status
- Shared, cheaply cloneable view of a connection’s current state.
- [Consumer](https://docs.rs/struct.Consumer.html)
- Continuously consumes message from a Queue.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)
- The error that can be returned in this crate.
- [Publisher](https://docs.rs/struct.PublisherConfirm.html)- Confirm
- A future that resolves to the broker’s acknowledgement of a published message.
- [Queue](https://docs.rs/struct.Queue.html)
- Information about an AMQP queue as returned by the server.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Async](https://docs.rs/enum.AsyncTcpStream.html)- TcpStream
- Wrapper around plain or TLS async TCP streams
- [Channel](https://docs.rs/enum.ChannelState.html)- State
- The lifecycle state of an AMQP channel.
- [Confirmation](https://docs.rs/enum.Confirmation.html)
- The broker’s response to a published message.
- [Connection](https://docs.rs/enum.ConnectionState.html)- State
- The lifecycle state of an AMQP connection.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.ErrorKind.html)- Kind
- The type of error that can be returned in this crate.
- [Event](https://docs.rs/enum.Event.html)
- A connection-level event delivered via `Connection::events_listener`
- [Exchange](https://docs.rs/enum.ExchangeKind.html)- Kind
- The routing algorithm used by an AMQP exchange.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Connect](https://docs.rs/trait.Connect.html)
- Extension trait that lets URI types open a `Connection`
- [Consumer](https://docs.rs/trait.ConsumerDelegate.html)- Delegate
- Callback-based alternative to polling a `Consumer`

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Basic](https://docs.rs/type.BasicProperties.html)- Properties

- [Default](https://docs.rs/type.DefaultConnectionBuilder.html)- Connection - Builder
- A `ConnectionBuilder`
- [Result](https://docs.rs/type.Result.html)
- A std Result with a lapin::Error error type

# amq_protocol_types - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/amq-protocol-types

## Expand description

AMQP 0-9-1 type system for Rust.

Implements the full set of AMQP scalar types ([ AMQPValue](https://docs.rs/enum.AMQPValue.html),

[), compound types (](https://docs.rs/enum.AMQPType.html)

`AMQPType`[,](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldTable.html)

`FieldTable`[), and wire-format serialisation/deserialisation via the](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldArray.html)

`FieldArray`[and](https://docs.rs/generation/index.html)

`generation`[modules.](https://docs.rs/parsing/index.html)

`parsing`## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [flags](https://docs.rs/flags/index.html)
- Helpers to handle AMQP flags.
- [generation](https://docs.rs/generation/index.html)
- Generation utilities for the various AMQP types.
- [parsing](https://docs.rs/parsing/index.html)
- Parsing utilities for the various AMQP types.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Byte](https://docs.rs/struct.ByteArray.html)- Array
- An array of bytes (RabbitMQ specific)
- [Decimal](https://docs.rs/struct.DecimalValue.html)- Value
- A Decimal value composed of a scale and a value
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldArray.html)- Array
- An array of AMQPValue
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldTable.html)- Table
- A Map<String, AMQPValue>
- [Long](https://docs.rs/struct.LongString.html)- String
- A String
- [Short](https://docs.rs/struct.ShortString.html)- String
- A String (deprecated)
- [Short](https://docs.rs/struct.ShortStringError.html)- String - Error
- Error returned when constructing a [ShortString](https://docs.rs/struct.ShortString.html)from a string that exceeds[MAX_SHORT_STRING_LENGTH](https://docs.rs/constant.MAX_SHORT_STRING_LENGTH.html)

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [AMQP](https://docs.rs/enum.AMQPType.html)- Type
- Enumeration referencing all the available AMQP types
- [AMQP](https://docs.rs/enum.AMQPValue.html)- Value
- Enumeration referencing the possible AMQP values depending on the types

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [MAX_](https://docs.rs/constant.MAX_SHORT_STRING_LENGTH.html)- SHORT_ - STRING_ - LENGTH
- Maximum byte length of a [ShortString](https://docs.rs/struct.ShortString.html)

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Boolean](https://docs.rs/type.Boolean.html)
- AMQP boolean (`t`): a single true/false value.
- [Channel](https://docs.rs/type.ChannelId.html)- Id
- A Channel identifier
- [Chunk](https://docs.rs/type.ChunkSize.html)- Size

- A delivery tag
- [Double](https://docs.rs/type.Double.html)

- [Float](https://docs.rs/type.Float.html)
- AMQP float (`f`): a 32-bit IEEE 754 floating-point value.
- [Frame](https://docs.rs/type.FrameSize.html)- Size
- the size of an AMQP frame
- [Heartbeat](https://docs.rs/type.Heartbeat.html)
- The maximum heartbeat interval
- [Identifier](https://docs.rs/type.Identifier.html)
- An identifier (class id or method id)
- [LongInt](https://docs.rs/type.LongInt.html)
- AMQP long-int (`I`): a signed 32-bit integer.
- [Long](https://docs.rs/type.LongLongInt.html)- Long - Int
- AMQP long-long-int (`L`): a signed 64-bit integer.
- [Long](https://docs.rs/type.LongLongUInt.html)- LongU - Int
- AMQP long-long-uint (`l`): an unsigned 64-bit integer.
- [LongU](https://docs.rs/type.LongUInt.html)- Int
- AMQP long-uint (`i`): an unsigned 32-bit integer.
- [Message](https://docs.rs/type.MessageCount.html)- Count
- The number of messages
- [Payload](https://docs.rs/type.PayloadSize.html)- Size
- The size of a delivery’s payload
- [Reply](https://docs.rs/type.ReplyCode.html)- Code
- A reply code (for closing channels and connections)
- [Short](https://docs.rs/type.ShortInt.html)- Int
- AMQP short-int (`U`): a signed 16-bit integer.
- [Short](https://docs.rs/type.ShortShortInt.html)- Short - Int
- AMQP short-short-int (`b`): a signed 8-bit integer.
- [Short](https://docs.rs/type.ShortShortUInt.html)- ShortU - Int
- AMQP short-short-uint (`B`): an unsigned 8-bit integer.
- [ShortU](https://docs.rs/type.ShortUInt.html)- Int
- AMQP short-uint (`u`): an unsigned 16-bit integer.
- [Timestamp](https://docs.rs/type.Timestamp.html)
- AMQP timestamp (`T`): a 64-bit POSIX timestamp (seconds since the Unix epoch).
- [Void](https://docs.rs/type.Void.html)
- AMQP void: the absence of a value, equivalent to `()`.

---

# amq_protocol_tcp - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/amq-protocol-tcp

## Expand description

TCP/TLS connection helpers for AMQP URIs.

Provides [ AMQPUriTcpExt](https://docs.rs/trait.AMQPUriTcpExt.html), a trait that extends

[with a](https://docs.rs/amq-protocol-uri/10.6.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/amq_protocol_uri/struct.AMQPUri.html)

`AMQPUri`[method that opens a](https://docs.rs/trait.AMQPUriTcpExt.html#method.connect)

`connect`[— with or without TLS — according to the URI scheme and the active runtime/TLS feature flags.](https://docs.rs/enum.TcpStream.html)

`TcpStream`[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature flags

[§](https://docs.rs#async-runtime-pick-exactly-one)Async runtime (pick exactly one)

| Flag | Notes |
|---|---|
| `tokio`(default) | Requires a running Tokio runtime |
| `smol` | Uses the smol executor |
| `async-global-executor` | Uses async-global-executor |

[§](https://docs.rs#tls-backend-pick-at-most-one-rustls-is-the-default)TLS backend (pick at most one; `rustls` is the default)

| Flag | Notes |
|---|---|
| `rustls`(default) | TLS via rustls |
| `native-tls` | TLS via the platform’s native library |
| `openssl` | TLS via OpenSSL |

[§](https://docs.rs#rustls-certificate-store-only-when-rustls-is-active)Rustls certificate store (only when `rustls` is active)

| Flag | Notes |
|---|---|
| `rustls-platform-verifier`(default) | Uses the platform trust store |
| `rustls-native-certs` | Loads native root certificates |
| `rustls-webpki-roots-certs` | Uses the webpki bundled root set |

[§](https://docs.rs#rustls-crypto-provider-at-least-one-must-be-enabled)Rustls crypto provider (at least one must be enabled)

| Flag | Notes |
|---|---|
| `rustls--aws_lc_rs`(default) | Uses aws-lc-rs |
| `rustls--ring` | Uses ring (more portable) |

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Native](https://docs.rs/struct.NativeTlsConnector.html)- TlsConnector
- A builder for client-side TLS connections.
- [Openssl](https://docs.rs/struct.OpensslConnector.html)- Connector
- A type which wraps client-side streams in a TLS session.
- [OwnedTLS](https://docs.rs/struct.OwnedTLSConfig.html)- Config
- Re-export TcpStream Holds extra TLS configuration
- [Rustls](https://docs.rs/struct.RustlsConnector.html)- Connector
- A rustls TLS connector ready to perform TLS handshakes.
- [Rustls](https://docs.rs/struct.RustlsConnectorConfig.html)- Connector - Config
- Configuration helper for `RustlsConnector`
- [TLSConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.TLSConfig.html)
- Re-export TcpStream Holds extra TLS configuration

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Async](https://docs.rs/enum.AsyncTcpStream.html)- TcpStream
- Re-export TcpStream Wrapper around plain or TLS async TCP streams
- [Handshake](https://docs.rs/enum.HandshakeError.html)- Error
- Re-export TcpStream An error returned while performing the handshake
- [Identity](https://docs.rs/enum.Identity.html)
- Re-export TcpStream Holds one of:
- [MidHandshake](https://docs.rs/enum.MidHandshakeTlsStream.html)- TlsStream
- Re-export TcpStream A TLS stream which has been interrupted during the handshake
- [Owned](https://docs.rs/enum.OwnedIdentity.html)- Identity
- Re-export TcpStream Holds one of:
- [TcpStream](https://docs.rs/enum.TcpStream.html)
- Re-export TcpStream Wrapper around plain or TLS TCP streams

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [AMQP](https://docs.rs/trait.AMQPUriTcpExt.html)- UriTcp - Ext
- Trait providing a method to connect to a TcpStream

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Handshake](https://docs.rs/type.HandshakeResult.html)- Result
- Re-export TcpStream
Holds either the TLS `TcpStream`result or the current handshake state
